================================================================
CUBRID PR <-> TC Branch Transaction: Implementation Summary
================================================================

COMPLETED (this session)
----------------------------------------------------------------
File: .github/workflows/tc-branch-sync.yml
  - Trigger: pull_request_target (opened, reopened, synchronize)
  - Creates tc/pr-<N> branch in both TC repos from develop
  - Skips silently if branch already exists
  - On failure: posts a comment on the Engine PR

File: .github/workflows/tc-branch-finalize.yml
  - Trigger: pull_request_target (closed)
  - If merged:   merges tc/pr-<N> into develop in both TC repos,
                 then deletes tc/pr-<N>
                 On conflict/failure: posts a comment on the Engine PR
  - If rejected: deletes tc/pr-<N> from both TC repos

================================================================
SETUP REQUIRED BEFORE WORKFLOWS CAN RUN
================================================================

1. Create a GitHub App in the CUBRID organization:
   - Go to: https://github.com/organizations/CUBRID/settings/apps
   - Set the following repository permission: Contents: Write
   - Install the App on both TC repos:
       CUBRID/cubrid-testcases
       CUBRID/cubrid-testcases-private-ex

2. Add the following two secrets to CUBRID/cubrid:
     Settings -> Secrets -> Actions

     Secret name : TC_APP_ID
     Secret value: <the GitHub App's numeric App ID>

     Secret name : TC_APP_PRIVATE_KEY
     Secret value: <the GitHub App's private key (full PEM content)>

   The workflows use actions/create-github-app-token@v1 to exchange
   these credentials for a short-lived installation token at runtime.

================================================================
REMAINING CI WORK (to be done manually)
================================================================

Modify the existing CI workflow(s) that checkout TC repos so they
use the tc/pr-<N> branch when available, falling back to develop.

In every step that clones a TC repo, replace the fixed branch
with the following shell logic:

  PR_BRANCH="tc/pr-${GITHUB_PULL_REQUEST_NUMBER}"
  # or: tc/pr-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}

  if git ls-remote --exit-code --heads \
       https://github.com/CUBRID/cubrid-testcases.git \
       "${PR_BRANCH}" 2>/dev/null; then
    TC_BRANCH="${PR_BRANCH}"
  else
    TC_BRANCH="develop"
  fi

  git clone -b "${TC_BRANCH}" \
    https://github.com/CUBRID/cubrid-testcases.git

Apply the same logic to cubrid-testcases-private-ex.

Additionally, to block Engine PR merges when TC has a conflict
(preventing the state where engine is merged but TC cannot merge),
add a merge-dry-run check inside CI:

  cd cubrid-testcases
  git fetch origin develop:develop
  git merge --no-commit --no-ff develop || {
    echo "TC branch conflicts with develop. Resolve before merging."
    git merge --abort
    exit 1
  }
  git merge --abort

This makes CI fail when a TC conflict exists, so GitHub branch
protection rules (require status checks to pass) will prevent
the Engine PR from being merged until the conflict is resolved.

================================================================
FUTURE ENHANCEMENTS (not yet implemented)
================================================================

1. Auto-sync develop into tc/pr-<N>
   When a developer merges develop into their Engine PR branch,
   automatically merge the latest develop into the corresponding
   TC branch as well.
   Approach: on synchronize event, detect if the new HEAD commit
   is a merge commit with develop as a parent, then merge develop
   into tc/pr-<N>.

2. Revert automation
   When a merged Engine PR is reverted (new PR with title starting
   with 'Revert ...'), detect the original PR number and create a
   matching revert in the TC repos.
   Current behavior: tc-branch-sync.yml creates a fresh tc/pr-<N>
   branch. A bot comment is NOT yet posted to remind about TC revert.
   Consider adding a revert-detection step to tc-branch-sync.yml.
